name: The Dupont Circle
positioning: The Dupont Circle Hotel, a Doyle Collection hotel in the Dupont Circle neighborhood of Washington D.C., with a mid-century aesthetic and a floor of penthouse suites
best_for: Travelers who want a central Dupont Circle base close to the Metro
Guests wanting a penthouse suite with a private terrace and city views

facts.text: The hotel sits in the center of the historic Dupont Circle neighborhood, a short stroll from the city's monuments.
Dupont Circle is a stylish diplomatic neighborhood.
The hotel is less than a two-minute walk from the Dupont Circle Metro Station.
The design blends contemporary comfort with a mid-century aesthetic that pays homage to the building's beginnings.
Guest rooms and suites blend art-forward design with modern comforts.
The ninth-floor penthouse level is reached by a private elevator.
The lobby has space to work or read by the fireplace.
Nightly turndown service and room service are available.
Service centers on welcoming Irish hospitality.
The hotel is owned and managed by The Doyle Collection, an Irish family-owned hotel group.
Doyle Bar has views of Dupont Circle and nods to the cocktail culture of the 1950s and 60s.
Doyle Bar has a collection of Irish whiskeys.

highlights.text: Suites with private furnished terraces have panoramic city views from the Washington Monument to the National Cathedral.
The Grand Penthouse was designed by Irish-born designer Clodagh and has five private heated terraces.
The hotel was refurbished in collaboration with designers Martin Brudnizki and Clodagh.
Bathrooms have marble tiles, heated floors and Malin + Goetz bath products.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes that nothing about the elegant, upscale property feels overly family-friendly.
WhataHotel notes limited parking availability in a busy urban setting.
